texts: An anomalous right subclavian artery arising from the descending thoracic aorta can be ligated and divided in the setting of interrupted aortic arch: B.
Dividing it frees the descending aorta, so it can be brought up and joined to the ascending aorta without tension.

The right ventricle is connected to the pulmonary arteries with a valved conduit, usually a homograft; the fundamental goal is to separate the two circulations, and a leaking truncal valve is repaired only when needed.
Mobilizing the descending aorta well, and avoiding tension, protects the left main bronchus from compression.
In the picture, the jester's sneaking flipper pipe is tied and cut, and the two halves of the orca are joined.
Memory hook: cut the jester's pipe, and the orca's halves meet.
